title: Local cohomological dimension does not increase under change of rings
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal. The extended ideal $IB$ is the ideal generated by $f(I)$. For an ideal $K$ of a commutative Noetherian ring $R$, put $\Gamma_K(M)=\{x\in M:K^nx=0\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$ and $H_K^j(M)=R^j\Gamma_K(M)$, the right derived functors on $R$-modules. Write $\operatorname{cd}(R,K)$ for the least integer $q\geq-1$ such that $H_K^j(M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$ and every $j>q$. Then $\operatorname{cd}(B,IB)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$. No flatness hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DXA (lemma-cd-change-rings), the inequality, restricted to Noetherian source and target rings so that local cohomology is also the right-derived ideal-torsion functor.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose a finite list $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ generating $I$. Put $u_i=f(t_i)$. The elements $u_i$ generate $J=IB$: each $a\in I$ is a sum $\sum a_it_i$, hence $f(a)=\sum f(a_i)u_i$, and each $u_i$ itself is in $f(I)$. This also handles $r=0$, when $I=0$ and $J=0$.

Let $N$ be an arbitrary $B$-module and write $N_A$ for the same additive group with $a\cdot n=f(a)n$. Both coefficient rings are Noetherian. Apply [lem-per-ideal-torsion-cech-computation] to $(A,(t_i),N_A)$ and to $(B,(u_i),N)$. Thus $H_I^j(N_A)$ and $H_J^j(N)$ are respectively the cohomology of $C_A(t_1,\ldots,t_r;N_A)$ and $C_B(u_1,\ldots,u_r;N)$. The same computation for any ideal of either ring, using a finite generating list of length $s$, makes every cohomology in degrees $>s$ zero, since the displayed complex has zero terms there. Consequently the least integers defining both cohomological dimensions exist (the nonempty set of admissible integers is bounded below by $-1$).

source.place: Tag 0956 (lemma-compute-local-cohomology-noetherian); local-cohomology.tex Tags 0DX8 (definition-cd) and 0DX9 (lemma-bound-cd), existence of the finite bound.

proof.text: For every nonempty ordered subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $t_S=\prod_{i\in S}t_i$ and $u_S=f(t_S)=\prod_{i\in S}u_i$. Identify $(N_A)_{t_S}$ with $(N_{u_S})_A$ by $n/t_S^a\mapsto n/u_S^a$, with inverse given by the reverse formula. In the fraction definition in [lem-per-ideal-torsion-cech-computation], the equality test on the first side is $t_S^c(t_S^b n-t_S^a n')=0$ in $N_A$, which is exactly $u_S^c(u_S^b n-u_S^a n')=0$ in $N$. Thus both maps are well-defined and inverse, including $u_S=0$. They preserve addition and the restricted $A$-action. They commute with every face localization: both ways send $n/t_S^a$ to the same fraction after additionally inverting the missing generator. Applying them componentwise, and the identity in degree zero, gives an $A$-linear cochain isomorphism of the two complexes in Step 2 after restriction of scalars. The alternating signs agree because the index order is unchanged. Kernels and images of a $B$-linear map are the same subsets after restricting scalars, and their quotient additive groups agree. Taking cohomology therefore identifies $H_I^j(N_A)$ with $(H_J^j(N))_A$ for every $j\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 0BJB (lemma-local-cohomology-and-restriction), second proof, with the fraction identification and compatibility with differentials written out.

proof.text: Put $q=\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$. If $j>q$ is a nonnegative degree, the defining vanishing property gives $H_I^j(N_A)=0$. Step 3 then says that the underlying additive group of $H_J^j(N)$ is zero, so this $B$-module is zero. Since $N$ was arbitrary, $q$ is admissible in the definition of $\operatorname{cd}(B,J)$, and its least admissible integer is at most $q$. This applies also to $q=-1$, when all nonnegative cohomology vanishes. For $r=0$ Step 3 is the identity of the degree-zero complexes. If either ring is zero, its modules are zero and the same argument applies. No tensoring of an exact sequence with $B$ and no flatness of $f$ was used.
